text: [BLOCKER] The "binding-loop peptides" do not occur in the proteins they are attributed to — every claimed natural-sequence provenance is false — I searched each peptide, and its interior core substring, against the actual UniProt sequence of the protein it is credited to. Zero matches in every case. "BDNF Loop-5" CVDRENPVEWVRAC does not appear anywhere in human BDNF (P23560; mature chain HSDPARRGELSVCDSISEWVTAADKKTAVDMSGGTVTVLEKVPVSKGQLKQYFYETKCNPMGYTKEGCRGIDKRHWNSQCRTTQSYVRALTMDSKKRIGWRFIRIDTSCVCTLTIKRGR) — and neurotrophins have four beta-hairpin loops (L1-L4), so "Loop-5" is not a structure that exists. "NGF Loop-1" EPKHVNCDRENP is absent from NGF (P01138). "Trem2 Peptide" GRLVGHPWECDR is absent from TREM2 (Q9NZC2). "alpha-7 nAChR ECD Peptide" SEAEFRLFRDVW is absent from CHRNA7 (P36544). Two peptides are degraded copies of real motifs rather than absent: the "Wnt3a Loop" CKCHGMSGSCSTKTCWWG is a corrupted version of the genuine WNT3A segment CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP at position 203 (L->M, EVK->STK, plus an illegal residue B), and the "Nrf2 ETGE" DEETGEFLFQLP is a mangled version of the real Nrf2 Neh2 sequence DEETGEFLPIQP at residues 77-88 of NFE2L2 (Q16236) — first eight residues correct, tail scrambled. The cysteine spacing of the recurring "TrkB" peptides (…CPTGKCEGLRGYTCRCEPGWKGPDCRERACPDCH, app.js:205) is EGF-like-repeat architecture, which is not found anywhere in TrkB — TrkB-d5 is an Ig-like C2-set domain with no such cysteine ladder. Consequence: The entire premise of Section 2 of the README is that the 25 candidates were built by "fusing minimal natural product pharmacophore warheads with AlphaFold3-optimized binding loop peptides" derived from the endogenous ligands. If the loops are not from the ligands, there is no rational basis for any of the binding claims, and a reader with a real target-validation budget could spend months and a five- to six-figure peptide-synthesis and SPR campaign chasing sequences that have no relationship to the receptors named. A pharmacologist skimming the README would reasonably assume "BDNF Loop-5" and "NGF Loop-1" are literature-sourced epitopes; both are inventions.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-01: Delete every claimed natural-sequence provenance that cannot be reproduced by an exact substring search against the cited UniProt accession, or replace each peptide with the genuine segment plus its UniProt accession and residue range (e.g. "Nrf2 76-88, Q16236, LDEETGEFLPIQ"). Add an automated CI check that, for every entry declaring a source protein, fetches that UniProt sequence and asserts the substring is present; fail the build otherwise. The .agents/skills/uniprot-database and ncbi-sequence-fetch skills already in this repo do exactly this.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-01: Neurotrophin receptor-binding determinants are known experimentally. BDNF/NT-4 engage TrkB through the membrane-proximal Ig-like domain d5 (Ultsch et al., PDB 1WWB, J Mol Biol 1999; Banfield et al., NT-4/5:TrkB-d5 complex, PDB 1HCF, Structure 2001), and the epitope is discontinuous — formed by beta-hairpin loops L1/L2/L4 and the N-terminal segment across both protomers of the disulfide-linked cystine-knot dimer. It cannot be reduced to one linear 14-mer. Wnt engages the Frizzled CRD principally through a palmitoleoyl lipid on a serine at the tip of the Wnt "thumb" inserting into a hydrophobic CRD groove, plus an "index finger" contact (Janda et al., Science 2012, PDB 4F0A) — a synthetic peptide cannot reproduce a covalently lipidated interface. The genuine Nrf2 Keap1-binding motif is the DxETGE beta-hairpin at Nrf2 77-88 (Lo et al., EMBO J 2006, PDB 2FLU).

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: [BLOCKER] Four peptide sequences are byte-identical but assigned to unrelated targets with different binding energies, proving no per-target computation was performed — I extracted all 25 sequences programmatically and grouped them. Four sequences each appear twice. Two of the duplicates are assigned to the SAME target (AChE) yet carry different dG and Kd — an identical molecule against an identical enzyme cannot have two affinities. The other three duplicates are assigned to structurally and functionally unrelated targets: a receptor tyrosine kinase Ig domain versus a SLC1-family membrane transporter; a Cys-loop receptor extracellular domain versus a TLR4/MD-2 leucine-rich-repeat complex; a Frizzled cysteine-rich domain versus an intracellular MAGUK scaffold (ZO-1) that a secreted peptide could not physically reach. Each pairing carries a different, precisely stated nanomolar Kd. Consequence: This is internal proof that no docking, no free-energy calculation, and no target-specific structure prediction was ever run. The numbers in the affinity fields — which drive the leaderboard (app.js:869-895), the benchmark bar chart (app.js:1049-1103), and the README's headline "-19.5 kcal/mol Peak Binding Energy" — are literary, not computational. Any collaborator or investor reading the pipeline as a triaged candidate list is being shown a ranking with no underlying measurement.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-02: Make every sequence unique per target, or, if reuse is intentional, state it explicitly and report one measured/computed affinity per (ligand, target) pair from a named method (e.g. Rosetta ddG, MM-GBSA, FoldX, or an experimental SPR value) with the software version and inputs. Add a uniqueness assertion over the sequence field and a consistency assertion that dG and Kd satisfy dG = RT ln(Kd) within stated error.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-02: A binding free energy is a property of a specific complex. For a single ligand and a single receptor at fixed conditions there is exactly one dG and one Kd, related by dG = RT ln(Kd); at 298 K, RT = 0.592 kcal/mol, so Kd = 2.1 nM corresponds to dG = -11.8 kcal/mol and Kd = 0.65 nM to dG = -12.4 kcal/mol — neither matches the -16.2 and -17.5 stated, and the stated pair is not even self-consistent with the stated Kd pair. Cross-reactivity of a single peptide against unrelated folds at low-nanomolar affinity is essentially unprecedented and, if real, would be reported as a serious selectivity liability rather than as five separate optimised drugs.

text: [CRITICAL] AChE binding sites mix Torpedo californica and human residue numbering inside the same string — I tested each residue against both sequences. In human AChE (UniProt P22303, mature numbering, signal peptide 1-31 removed), position 84 is Glu, 330 is Val, 121 is Gly, and 279 is Gln — none of the claimed residues exists. In Torpedo californica AChE (P04058, mature numbering, signal 1-21 removed), positions 84/330/121/279 are exactly Trp/Phe/Tyr/Trp. So "Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121, Trp279" is Torpedo numbering. Meanwhile "Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr341" and Asp74 are correct human residues (all verified against P22303). app.js:154 therefore describes the catalytic anionic site of an electric-ray enzyme and the peripheral anionic site of the human enzyme as if they were one protein, and app.js:12 compounds the error by pairing Torpedo Trp279 with the human Trp286 elsewhere in the same file — these are the same residue in two species, listed as if they were two distinct sites. A secondary error: app.js:12 labels the Trp84/Phe330 interaction a "CAS Salt Bridge," but app.js:15 correctly calls the same interaction cation-pi. Aromatic residues cannot form salt bridges; the gorge has no anionic site in the classical sense (this was the central finding of the 1991 Torpedo structure). Consequence: A reader designing a mutagenesis experiment, a docking grid, or a selectivity assay against human AChE would build W84A/F330A constructs that do not exist, or centre a docking box on the wrong coordinates. Species numbering confusion in the AChE literature is a classic, well-documented trap, and publishing a "human AChE" target sheet in Torpedo numbering propagates it. Because five of the 25 candidates (X2, B1, B4, B5, and the bispecific CogDual-TrkB-PAS-10) are AChE-directed, the error contaminates a fifth of the pipeline.

text: Required fix for MOLBIO-03: Pick one convention, state it explicitly ("human AChE, UniProt P22303, mature numbering"), and convert consistently: Trp84->Trp86, Phe330->Tyr337, Tyr121->Tyr124, Trp279->Trp286. Correct "CAS Salt Bridge" to "cation-pi" at app.js:12. Where a structure is cited in Torpedo numbering (e.g. 1VOT), give both, e.g. "Trp86 (human; Trp84 in Torpedo, PDB 1VOT)".

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-03: Human AChE (P22303) mature numbering: catalytic triad Ser203/Glu334/His447; CAS/acyl pocket aromatics Trp86 (the cation-pi anchor for the quaternary ammonium), Tyr337, Tyr124, Phe295/Phe297; PAS at the gorge mouth Trp286, Tyr72, Tyr124, Asp74, Tyr341. The Torpedo equivalents are Trp84, Phe330, Tyr121, Trp279, Tyr70, Asp72, Tyr334. Note that Torpedo Phe330 maps to human Tyr337, not to a phenylalanine, so a naive renumbering would still be wrong. The gorge aromatics, not an anionic site, bind the quaternary ammonium (Sussman et al., Science 1991, PMID 1678899). Huperzine A binding is resolved in PDB 1VOT (Raves et al., Nat Struct Biol 1997), in Torpedo numbering.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: [CRITICAL] A 36-mer polycationic peptide cannot clamp both the AChE CAS and PAS, and the claimed "complete blockade with zero seizure risk" inverts cholinergic toxicology — Two separate errors. (i) Steric: the AChE active-site gorge is roughly 20 Angstroms deep, narrow, and lined with aromatics, with a bottleneck of a few Angstroms; the catalytic serine sits near its base. A 36-residue peptide with a formal charge of about +9 and four tryptophans cannot thread that gorge to contact Trp86/Tyr337 while simultaneously occupying the PAS at the mouth. The definitive precedent is fasciculin-2, a 61-residue three-finger toxin that inhibits AChE almost completely by capping the PAS and occluding the gorge entrance — it does not, and cannot, reach the catalytic site (PDB 1FSS, Bourne et al., Structure 1995). A peptide of this class is a PAS blocker, full stop. (ii) Pharmacological: "complete" blockade of ACh degradation with "+350% synaptic ACh," "no peripheral side effects," and a seizure index of 0.01 is not an achievable safety profile — it is the described mechanism of organophosphate and carbamate poisoning. Near-total AChE inhibition produces cholinergic crisis: status epilepticus, bronchorrhoea, bradycardia, and respiratory failure. The platform asserts maximal target engagement and zero on-target toxicity simultaneously, which is a contradiction in terms for this target. Consequence: AChE is the single most safety-constrained target in the cholinergic pharmacopoeia, and the therapeutic index is defined by submaximal, titrated inhibition. A document that presents "complete blockade" as a design goal and pairs it with a fabricated near-zero seizure index would, if acted on, drive dose escalation toward the exact toxicity the field spends its effort avoiding. This is the finding with the clearest path to physical harm if the platform were ever used to inform dosing or candidate selection.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-04: Reclassify X2, B1, B4 and B5 as PAS-directed ligands only, and delete the CAS engagement claim for all peptide-only constructs (a small-molecule warhead conjugated on a linker could plausibly reach the CAS, but that requires an explicit linker-length calculation, not an assertion). Replace "completely blocks" and "+350% ACh" with a target inhibition range consistent with a therapeutic index (e.g. 40-80% enzyme inhibition) and remove the fabricated seizure indices entirely until a real convulsant-liability assessment exists. Add an explicit on-target cholinergic-toxicity section citing the organophosphate precedent.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-04: Clinically, cholinesterase inhibition in Alzheimer's disease is deliberately submaximal and plateaus: donepezil showed a red-blood-cell AChE inhibition plateau of 76-84% at plasma concentrations above 50 ng/mL, with efficacy correlated to that inhibition and dose limited by cholinergic adverse events (Rogers & Friedhoff, Dementia 1996, PMID 8915035). On-target dose-limiting effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, bradycardia and syncope; supratherapeutic inhibition causes seizures. Separately, the PAS is a legitimate and valuable target in its own right: PAS ligands block AChE-catalysed acceleration of Abeta fibril assembly (Inestrosa et al., Neuron 1996, PMID 8608006), which is exactly the secondary mechanism the platform claims — so the PAS half of the design is sound and should be kept.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: [CRITICAL] TrkB d5 domain is correctly identified but four of six named binding residues are the wrong amino acids, and the "BDNF Loop-5 dimerizer" concept ignores the reproducibility record of TrkB agonist pharmacology — The domain assignment is right and deserves credit: UniProt Q16620 annotates Ig-like C2-type 2 (the d5 domain, in the standard d1-d5 Trk nomenclature) at residues 295-365, so residues 298-342 do fall inside it. But the residue identities mostly do not check out. Against Q16620 full-length numbering: 298 is Asp (correct), 342 is Tyr (correct), but 319 is Tyr not Glu, 315 is Leu not Thr, 312 is Lys not Val, and 333 is Lys not Leu. Two of six correct is what random guessing constrained to the right domain would give. I also tested mature numbering (signal peptide 1-31 removed, offset +31): zero of six match, so the errors are not a numbering-convention artefact. Separately, "Glu319" is asserted as a BDNF-contact residue in four places, but there is no experimental BDNF-TrkB complex structure to derive it from — a PDB full-text search returns 1WWB (apo human TrkB ligand-binding domain), 1HCF (NT-4/5 bound to TrkB-d5), 5MO9 (TrkB LBD with an antibody Fab), and kinase-domain entries, but no BDNF-TrkB complex. Consequence: Anyone attempting to validate the design would order D298A/E319A TrkB constructs; E319A is not a mutation of the residue the platform thinks it is targeting, and the resulting negative result would be uninterpretable. More broadly, presenting a linear peptide as a "TrkB dimerizer" without engaging the field's reproducibility history is misleading to a non-specialist reader: several widely used "small-molecule TrkB agonists" failed to activate TrkB in rigorous multiplexed assays, and the field now regards claimed TrkB agonism as requiring unusually strong controls.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-05: Replace the invented residue list with contacts read directly from PDB 1HCF (NT-4/5:TrkB-d5) and state the source and numbering convention, or drop the residue list and say only "TrkB d5 (Q16620, residues 295-365)". Remove the claim that a monovalent linear peptide induces TrkB dimerisation, or support it with a stated bivalent architecture and a dimerisation assay design. Add an explicit caveat citing Boltaev et al. 2017 wherever TrkB agonism is claimed.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-05: Human TrkB (NTRK2, Q16620): LRRNT 32-61, LRR1 92-113, LRR2 116-137, LRRCT 148-196, Ig-like C2-type 1 (d4) 197-282, Ig-like C2-type 2 (d5) 295-365, kinase 538-807. d5 is the principal neurotrophin-binding domain (Ultsch et al., PDB 1WWB, J Mol Biol 1999; Banfield et al., NT-4/5:TrkB-d5, PDB 1HCF, Structure 2001). Boltaev et al. (Sci Signal 2017, PMID 28831019) developed complementary quantitative assays of TrkB phosphorylation, downstream signalling and gene expression and could not reproduce receptor activation by the reported small-molecule TrkB agonists, concluding that results obtained with these compounds must be interpreted with caution. Zagrebelsky & Korte (Neural Regen Res 2024, PMID 37488840) review the current TrkB-agonist landscape and note that agonist antibodies — which are bivalent and can genuinely crosslink the receptor — are the more credible modality, while questioning whether any TrkB agonist reverses pathology per se.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: [CRITICAL] Two candidates are labelled positive allosteric modulators while the residues listed for them are the orthosteric agonist sites, and the real alpha-7 PAM site is inaccessible to a peptide — The residues are real — I verified Tyr188, Trp149 and Tyr195 against CHRNA7 (P36544) mature numbering and Tyr381/Trp164 against CHRM1 (P11229) — but they are the wrong kind of site for the stated mechanism. Trp149 (loop B) and Tyr188/Tyr195 (loop C) are the canonical aromatic box of the alpha-7 ORTHOSTERIC acetylcholine binding site; a ligand occupying them is an agonist or competitive antagonist, definitionally not a PAM. Likewise M1 Tyr381 is part of the orthosteric tyrosine lid (with Tyr106, Tyr404, Tyr408, Asp105), not the allosteric vestibule. A second, independent problem: the best-characterised alpha-7 type-II PAM site is an intrasubunit cavity in the transmembrane domain, buried in the lipid bilayer — a 41-residue hydrophilic peptide cannot reach it. And PAM activity requires modulating the agonist-induced gating equilibrium without occupying the agonist site, which a peptide sitting in the aromatic box would preclude by construction. Consequence: PAM versus orthosteric agonist is the single most consequential distinction in cholinergic drug design for cognition: PAMs preserve the temporal and spatial pattern of endogenous ACh release and avoid the receptor desensitisation and peripheral cholinergic toxicity that sank orthosteric alpha-7 and M1 agonist programmes. A document that labels an orthosteric-site binder a PAM, and then asserts "Receptor Desensitization: Low" (app.js:199) as a consequence, gets the safety rationale exactly backwards — orthosteric alpha-7 agonism causes rapid, profound desensitisation.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-06: Either relabel P1 and B2 as orthosteric ligands and rewrite their mechanism and desensitisation claims accordingly, or keep the PAM label and replace the residue lists with genuine allosteric-site residues (alpha-7 intrasubunit TMD cavity; M1 extracellular vestibule) — and in that case explain how a peptide reaches an intramembrane cavity, which for alpha-7 it cannot. Remove "Receptor Desensitization: Low" until it is supported by a stated assay.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-06: For alpha-7, PNU-120596 potentiates without altering the orthosteric agonist binding site; the modulation is transduced through a network of gating-interface and transmembrane residues (Marotta, Lester & Dougherty, Chem Biol 2015, PMID 26211363). Docking and MD analyses place type-II PAMs including PNU-120596 in an intrasubunit transmembrane cavity, with M1-Ser223 and M3-Ile281 as key contacts, and type-I PAMs at an ECD or ECD-TMD junction site (Targowska-Duda et al., J Biomol Struct Dyn 2018, PMID 29363414). For muscarinic receptors, the common allosteric site is the extracellular vestibule above the orthosteric pocket, structurally defined for M2 with LY2119620 (PDB 4MQT, Nature 2013) and for M1/M4 orthosteric architecture in PDB 5CXV (Thal et al., Nature 2016).

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: [CRITICAL] Efficacy magnitudes (+280% LTP, +310% spine density, +350% ACh, +420% phagocytosis) are dimensionally undefined and, read literally, describe pathology rather than cognitive enhancement — None of these numbers is a well-formed quantity. LTP is conventionally reported as fEPSP slope or amplitude as a percentage OF baseline (e.g. 150-200% of baseline after theta-burst stimulation in CA1), so "+280%" is ambiguous between "180% of baseline" and "380% of baseline"; the latter exceeds what CA1 Schaffer-collateral synapses can express. Worse, more LTP is not monotonically better: potentiation saturates, and saturated hippocampal LTP impairs rather than improves learning, because there is no residual dynamic range left to encode new information. "Spine density +310%" is physically implausible — CA1 pyramidal basal and apical oblique dendrites carry roughly 1-3 spines per micrometre; a 4.1-fold increase implies 4-12 spines per micrometre, beyond the geometric packing limit of the dendritic shaft, and pathological spine overproduction is a feature of fragile X and related synaptopathies, not of enhanced cognition. "Working memory span +240%" is not a defined psychometric operation on a span score. All of these are stated with no assay, no species, no n, no baseline, no variance, and no statistic. Consequence: These figures are the platform's headline efficacy claims and appear in the README's public-facing summary. Presented without units or method they read as spectacular preclinical data; interpreted correctly by a slice electrophysiologist or a spine morphometrist they are either meaningless or describe a lesion. A reader budgeting a validation study cannot design a powered experiment against an endpoint that has no operational definition, and a reader who takes them at face value would conclude the compounds have been characterised in vivo when nothing has been measured at all.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-07: For every efficacy number: state the assay (e.g. "fEPSP slope, Schaffer collateral-CA1, 60 min post-TBS, acute mouse hippocampal slice"), the units and referent ("% of pre-tetanus baseline"), species, n, and dispersion — or delete the number. Replace open-ended "+X%" framing with a target range bounded by physiology and an explicit statement of the saturation/occlusion ceiling for LTP, citing Moser et al. 1998. Cap spine-density claims at biologically attainable densities.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-07: Realistic effect sizes: theta-burst or high-frequency-induced CA1 LTP typically reaches 130-200% of baseline fEPSP slope, with strong protocols approaching 200-250%; a pharmacological enhancer that raises potentiation by 20-50% relative to vehicle is a large, publishable effect. Saturation of hippocampal LTP impairs spatial learning — rats with less than 10% residual potentiation were disrupted in the water maze while those retaining capacity for further potentiation were not (Moser, Krobert, Moser & Morris, Science 1998, PMID 9748165) — so maximising LTP is not a coherent therapeutic objective. Spine density changes reported for genuine plasticity manipulations are typically 10-40%. Microdialysis studies of cholinesterase inhibitors report hippocampal/cortical ACh increases in the range of roughly 100-500% of basal, but that is a percentage OF basal in a specific compartment, not a compound-wide constant, and it must be reconciled with the cholinergic toxicity ceiling.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: [MAJOR] The M1/M2 microglial polarization dichotomy organising an entire brain-region module was formally deprecated by the field a decade ago — The whole fourth region of the pipeline is built on a binary classification that the microglial field has explicitly rejected. M1/M2 was borrowed from in vitro macrophage stimulation paradigms (LPS/IFN-gamma versus IL-4) and never mapped onto microglial biology in vivo; single-cell transcriptomics instead reveals a continuum of context-dependent states (disease-associated microglia, white-matter-associated microglia, interferon-responsive, proliferative-region-associated, and others) that do not resolve into two poles and that decouple "inflammatory" from "non-phagocytic". Framing therapeutic success as "M1 to M2 transition" therefore describes a state change that cannot be measured, because the endpoint states are not real categories. A compounding presentational problem: the drugs in this module are named M1 through M5, so "MicroTrem2-Agonist-M1" is a drug called M1 whose stated purpose is to abolish M1 microglia, and "BasalM1-PAM-B2" uses M1 to mean the muscarinic receptor — three incompatible meanings of "M1" in one dataset. Consequence: Any experimental plan derived from this module would specify the wrong readouts — an iNOS/Arg1 or CD86/CD206 ratio rather than a state-resolved transcriptomic or functional panel — and would be rejected at review. In a therapeutic context the dichotomy is actively harmful because it implies that suppressing "M1" and promoting "M2" are the same axis, when TREM2-dependent disease-associated microglia are simultaneously highly activated and beneficial for plaque compaction. The naming collision would also cause real confusion in any downstream data table.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-08: Replace "M1/M2 polarization" throughout with state-and-function language consistent with the Paolicelli et al. 2022 recommendations — name the specific functional endpoint being targeted (e.g. "enhanced Abeta phagocytic capacity and lysosomal processing", "reduced IL-1beta/TNF-alpha release") and, where a transcriptional state is meant, name it (e.g. DAM/ARM signature). Cite Ransohoff 2016 and Paolicelli et al. 2022. Separately, rename the MicroDrugs M1-M5 series to avoid collision with muscarinic M1 and with the deprecated microglial M1 label.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-08: Ransohoff (Nat Neurosci 2016, PMID 27459405, "A polarizing question: do M1 and M2 microglia exist?") argues that microglial polarization was never established by research findings, that the schema was adopted as an interpretive convenience before microglial ontogeny was understood, and that the terminology now hinders rather than aids progress and should be discarded. Paolicelli et al. (Neuron 2022, PMID 36327895, "Microglia states and nomenclature: A field at its crossroads"), a consensus paper with ~90 authors including Stevens, Colonna, Haass, Prinz, de Strooper and Ransohoff, states that the dualistic good/bad classification is inconsistent with the repertoire of microglial states and provides a conceptual framework and explicit nomenclature recommendations for researchers, reviewers and editors.

text: [MAJOR] TREM2 agonism by a linear monovalent 12-mer is not a plausible mechanism, and the clinical precedent for TREM2 agonism is presented without its negative outcome — Three problems. (i) Mechanism: TREM2 signals through the ITAM-bearing adaptor DAP12, and receptor activation requires clustering/crosslinking so that Src-family kinases can trans-phosphorylate the ITAM and recruit SYK. A monovalent linear 12-mer binding one Ig domain cannot crosslink the receptor; at best it is a competitive ligand-site blocker, i.e. an antagonist. Every credible TREM2 agonist in development is bivalent (an IgG). (ii) Residues: I checked against Q9NZC2 — Arg47 and Asp87 are the correct amino acids at those positions and Arg47 is genuinely on the AD-risk functional surface (credit for that), but position 112 is Ser, not Lys, and 112 is the boundary of the Ig-like V-type domain (annotated 29-112). Asp87 is acidic, which is hard to reconcile with a ligand surface whose defining property is a basic patch that engages anionic lipids. (iii) Provenance: the peptide GRLVGHPWECDR does not occur in TREM2 or, per the design logic, in any TREM2 ligand — see MOLBIO-01. (iv) Framing: the README presents TREM2 agonism as a solved route to amyloid clearance with "Cytokine Storm Risk: Negligible", omitting that the only TREM2 agonist antibody to reach Phase 2 in AD failed and produced ARIA-like MRI findings. Consequence: TREM2 is one of the most consequential genetic targets in AD and one of the most heavily invested; a document asserting a nanomolar peptide agonist with negligible immune risk, and no mention of the clinical readout, materially misrepresents the state of the field to anyone using it for target prioritisation. The safety framing is the sharper problem: TREM2 agonism in patients was associated with ARIA-like imaging abnormalities, which is the opposite of "negligible" risk.

text: Required fix for MOLBIO-09: Either reclassify the TREM2 constructs as ligand-site binders of unknown functional sign (and remove "Agonist" from the name and "Promotes Trem2/DAP12 signaling" from the mechanism), or specify a bivalent/multimeric architecture and a defined clustering readout (SYK phosphorylation, pERK, or a reporter assay). Correct Lys112 to a real residue on the Kober functional surface and justify Asp87 against the published anionic-ligand-binding surface. Add the AL002 Phase 2 outcome and the ARIA-like safety signal wherever TREM2 agonism is presented, and delete "Cytokine Storm Risk: Negligible".

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-09: The TREM2 Ig-like V-type ectodomain structure identified a functional surface on which AD risk variants (including R47H) cluster and which mediates ligand binding, while Nasu-Hakola mutations are buried and destabilise the fold (Kober et al., eLife 2016, PMID 27995897, PDB 5ELI); a later structure resolved wild-type and R47H Ig domains including a phosphatidylserine complex, establishing anionic phospholipid as a direct ligand (PDB 5UD7, 6B8O, J Biol Chem 2018). Physiological TREM2 ligands are anionic and lipidic — phospholipids, sulfatide, lipoproteins and apolipoproteins, and Abeta oligomers — engaged via the basic surface patch. Clinically, the humanized TREM2 agonistic mAb AL002 in 381 participants with early AD showed sustained CNS target engagement (reduced CSF sTREM2, increased osteopontin) but did NOT meet its primary endpoint on CDR-SB at 96 weeks, and the most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events were MRI changes resembling ARIA (Mummery et al., Nat Med 2026, PMID 41787076, NCT04592874).

text: [MAJOR] The Keap1 module conflates two mechanistically distinct interventions in different domains, and the ETGE decoy strategy is presented without the hinge-and-latch constraint — though the Kelch residue set itself is correct — Credit first, because it is substantial: I verified Tyr334, Arg415, Arg483 and Ser602 against KEAP1 (Q14145) and all four are correct, and they are precisely the canonical Nrf2-ETGE hot-spot residues of the Kelch beta-propeller (the full published set also includes Arg380, Asn382, Asn414, Ser508, Ser555, Tyr572, all of which I confirmed as the stated amino acids). Cys151 is also correctly identified as a Keap1 cysteine at position 151. The problem is that the platform welds two different mechanisms into one. Cys151 sits in the BTB domain and works by disrupting Keap1-Cul3 E3 ligase function; an ETGE decoy peptide competes at the Kelch propeller for Nrf2 substrate binding. These are different domains, different pharmacology (covalent/irreversible versus reversible PPI competition), different selectivity liabilities, and different structure-activity requirements — index.html:230 collapses them into a single arrow. Second, the design ignores the two-site hinge-and-latch architecture: Nrf2 binds one Keap1 dimer through a high-affinity ETGE hinge and a low-affinity DLG latch, and it is disengagement of the DLG latch that blocks ubiquitin transfer. A monovalent ETGE-only decoy must outcompete the tightest of the two contacts and does not address the latch, which is why real Keap1-Nrf2 PPI programmes emphasise avidity and bivalency. Third, the peptide sequence is a corrupted copy of the real motif (DEETGEFLFQLP versus Nrf2's DEETGEFLPIQP at 77-88) — the DEETGE core survives, so it may still bind, but the design was not read off the actual sequence. Finally, curcumin's Cys151 selectivity is asserted flatly; Keap1 uses multiple cysteine sensors with inducer-specific preference, and curcumin is a promiscuous, redox-active, assay-interfering polyphenol. Consequence: A reader would design the wrong validation experiment: a Keap1 C151S rescue assay tests the BTB mechanism and tells you nothing about a Kelch-competitive decoy, and vice versa. The omission of the latch also means the decoy's predicted potency is systematically overstated. And because Nrf2 activation is a double-edged intervention — constitutive Nrf2 activation is oncogenic — a design document that treats "maximal Nrf2 release" as an unqualified good without a tumorigenicity discussion is incomplete for a chronic CNS indication.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Required fix for MOLBIO-10: Split the Keap1 mechanism into two clearly separated arms in both index.html:230 and the README: (a) BTB Cys151 covalent modification, with a stated Cys151-dependence experiment (Keap1 C151S rescue) and a cysteine-selectivity profile; and (b) Kelch-domain ETGE PPI competition, with the hinge-and-latch constraint stated and a bivalency/avidity rationale. Correct the decoy peptide to the true Nrf2 76-88 sequence or state explicitly that it is an engineered variant. Add a Nrf2-activation oncogenicity caveat citing Shibata et al. 2008. Keep the Kelch residue list as-is — it is correct.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-10: The Keap1 Kelch:Nrf2-ETGE interface is resolved at 1.5 Angstrom (Lo, Li, Bewley & Hannink, "Structure of the Keap1:Nrf2 interface provides mechanistic insight into Nrf2 signaling", EMBO J 2006, PDB 2FLU), and Tyr334/Arg415/Arg483/Ser602 are among its hot-spot contacts. The two-site hinge-and-latch model — ETGE as high-affinity hinge, DLG as low-affinity latch, both required for efficient ubiquitination — is set out in Tong, Kobayashi, Katsuoka & Yamamoto (Biol Chem 2006, PMID 17081101) and validated in vivo by cancer-associated NRF2 mutations that specifically disrupt DLG or ETGE and cause constitutive Nrf2 accumulation (Shibata et al., PNAS 2008, PMID 18757741) — the same paper establishing that constitutive Nrf2 activation confers chemoresistance and poor prognosis. Cys151 is one of several Keap1 sensor cysteines with inducer-specific dependence: tBHQ, diethylmaleate, sulforaphane and dimethylfumarate are Cys151-preferring, whereas 15d-PGJ2, CDDO-Im, ebselen, nitro-oleic acid and cadmium act through Cys151-independent routes (Takaya et al., Free Radic Biol Med 2012, PMID 22732183).

text: [MINOR] Two sequences contain a non-standard amino acid letter and one "sequence" field is not a sequence at all, so the advertised AlphaFold Server submission path cannot work for those entries — I validated every sequence character against the 20 standard amino acids. Three entries fail. Two contain the letter B, which is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx (Asp or Asn) and is not an assignable residue — AlphaFold Server rejects non-standard single-letter codes, so the one-click "Launch AlphaFold Server" path advertised at README.md:111 and index.html:363 cannot succeed for these candidates. The third entry's sequence field contains the literal string "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate", a description rather than a sequence; the modal will nonetheless render a 3D "backbone", a pLDDT curve and a PAE heatmap for it, because the rendering functions (app.js:707-773, 775-832, 834-866) index character codes without validating the input. Note this also means A4 has no molecule at all behind its stated Kd of 4.8 nM. In fairness, the derived B in the Wnt peptide traces to a real WNT3A segment (CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP) in which the corresponding position is L, so the fix is unambiguous. Consequence: It breaks the platform's one genuinely functional external integration and, more importantly, it demonstrates that no validation gate exists between the data table and the rendering layer — the same absence that lets a target-less description string produce a confident-looking pLDDT profile above 90.

text: Required fix for MOLBIO-11: Add a sequence validator that rejects any character outside ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY before an entry can be stored or rendered, and have the modal refuse to draw 3D/pLDDT/PAE panels for an invalid sequence rather than fabricating one. Correct the B in the Wnt-derived peptide (to L, per WNT3A P56704) and either supply a real sequence for AstroPafr-Block-A4 or mark it explicitly as a small-molecule-only candidate with no peptide component and no structural panels.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Ground truth for MOLBIO-11: The IUPAC-IUB single-letter amino acid alphabet assigns exactly 20 letters to standard residues (ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY); B is the ambiguity code for Asx (Asp or Asn), Z for Glx, J for Leu/Ile, and X for unknown. Structure predictors, including AlphaFold Server, require unambiguous standard residues (plus explicitly supported modifications) and reject ambiguity codes, because there is no defined side-chain chemistry to model. The genuine WNT3A residue at the corresponding position of the CKCHG motif is Leu (WNT3A P56704, segment CKCHGLSGSCEVKTCWWSQP beginning at residue 203).

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Atomic structure of acetylcholinesterase from Torpedo californica: a prototypic acetylcholine-binding protein (1991). The original AChE structure. Establishes the deep, narrow active-site gorge reaching halfway into the protein, the Ser-His-Glu triad, and that the quaternary ammonium is bound by gorge aromatics rather than a classical anionic site. It is also the origin of the Torpedo residue numbering (Trp84, Phe330, Trp279) that the platform mistakenly presents as human. Application here: Use it to fix MOLBIO-03: cite it explicitly as the Torpedo-numbering source and give the human P22303 equivalents alongside. Use the gorge geometry it reports as the quantitative basis for rejecting the CAS+PAS dual-clamp claim in MOLBIO-04.

source.ref: PDB 1FSS (Structure, 1995; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Crystal structure of an acetylcholinesterase-fasciculin complex: interaction of a three-fingered toxin from snake venom with its target (1995). The definitive precedent for how a peptide/protein ligand engages AChE: fasciculin-2, 61 residues, caps the peripheral anionic site and occludes the gorge mouth without reaching the catalytic site. Application here: Cite as the structural counterexample in MOLBIO-04. It shows that a peptide-class AChE ligand is a PAS blocker by necessity, and it also shows that PAS occlusion alone is sufficient for near-complete inhibition — so the redesign should keep the PAS mechanism and drop the CAS claim.

source.ref: PDB 1VOT (Nat Struct Biol, 1997; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Structure of acetylcholinesterase complexed with the nootropic alkaloid, (-)-huperzine A (1997). The experimental huperzine A binding mode in the AChE gorge, in Torpedo numbering. Application here: Replace the invented huperzine A contact list at app.js:12 (which mislabels the aromatic interaction a "salt bridge") with the actual contacts from this structure, stated in the correct numbering convention with the human equivalents given.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Acetylcholinesterase accelerates assembly of amyloid-beta-peptides into Alzheimer's fibrils: possible role of the peripheral site of the enzyme (1996). Establishes the non-catalytic, PAS-dependent pro-amyloidogenic activity of AChE (blocked by the PAS ligand propidium, unaffected by the active-site inhibitor edrophonium; butyrylcholinesterase, which lacks a PAS, is inactive). Application here: This is the strongest legitimate rationale the platform has for its PAS-directed candidates (X2, B4) and should be cited there. It also supplies the correct pharmacological logic for MOLBIO-04: target the PAS for the anti-amyloid effect rather than claiming maximal catalytic-site blockade.

source.ref: PDB 1WWB (J Mol Biol, 1999; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Crystal structures of the neurotrophin-binding domain of TrkA, TrkB and TrkC (1999). The apo structure of the human TrkB d5 ligand-binding domain, confirming that the neurotrophin-binding module is the membrane-proximal Ig-like domain. Application here: Confirms the platform's correct "TrkB Ig-like D5" nomenclature (credit this) and is the reference frame in which the incorrect residue identities of MOLBIO-05 should be corrected. Note for the authors: this entry is apo TrkB-d5, not a BDNF complex.

source.ref: PDB 1HCF (Structure, 2001; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Specificity in Trk-receptor:neurotrophin interaction: the crystal structure of TrkB-d5 in complex with neurotrophin-4/5 (2001). The only experimental TrkB ligand complex; defines the actual d5 contact residues and the specificity determinants of neurotrophin recognition. Application here: Use it to replace the fabricated "Asp298, Glu319, Tyr342, Val312, Leu333" list with real contacts. A PDB full-text search performed in this session returned no BDNF-TrkB complex, so this is the nearest experimental ground truth and that limitation should be stated in the README.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Multiplex quantitative assays indicate a need for reevaluating reported small-molecule TrkB agonists (2017). Complementary quantitative assays of TrkB receptor activation, downstream signalling and gene expression in multiple cellular contexts; BDNF gave robust dose-dependent responses while the reported small-molecule TrkB agonists did not reproduce them. Application here: Mandatory caveat wherever the platform claims TrkB agonism or dimerisation (MOLBIO-05). Also supplies the assay design any honest TrkB validation plan should adopt: multiplexed pTrkB, downstream pAKT/pERK, and transcriptional readout, with BDNF as the positive control.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Are TrkB receptor agonists the right tool to fulfill the promises for a therapeutic value of the brain-derived neurotrophic factor? (2024). Current review of the TrkB agonist landscape across modalities, with particular attention to agonist antibodies (bivalent, TrkB-selective, do not engage p75) as the more credible route, and a sober assessment that TrkB agonists are unlikely to reverse disease pathology per se. Application here: Use to reframe the TrkB candidates (X1, X5, P2, and CogBDNF-Mimic-04) around a modality that can actually dimerise the receptor, and to temper the neurogenesis/LTP efficacy language in README.md:60 and 64.

source.ref: PDB 2FLU (EMBO J, 2006; primary citation retrieved from the RCSB entry record in this session)

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Structure of the Keap1:Nrf2 interface provides mechanistic insight into Nrf2 signaling (2006). 1.5 Angstrom structure of the Keap1 Kelch beta-propeller bound to the Nrf2 Neh2 ETGE peptide, defining the hot-spot residues that the platform lists correctly. Application here: Cite it at app.js:164 to substantiate the (correct) Tyr334/Arg415/Arg483/Ser602 set, and use it as the template for correcting the ETGE decoy sequence to the genuine Nrf2 76-88 motif.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Two-site substrate recognition model for the Keap1-Nrf2 system: a hinge and latch mechanism (2006). The hinge-and-latch framework: the high-affinity ETGE hinge and low-affinity DLG latch jointly position Nrf2 for ubiquitination, and their differential redox sensitivity explains Keap1-dependent Nrf2 stabilisation. Application here: Directly constrains the "Keap1 decoy" design in MOLBIO-10: a monovalent ETGE-only peptide competes only at the hinge. Use it to motivate a bivalent or avidity-driven decoy and to set realistic potency expectations.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Cancer related mutations in NRF2 impair its recognition by Keap1-Cul3 E3 ligase and promote malignancy (2008). In vivo validation of the two-site model via somatic NRF2 DLG/ETGE mutations, plus evidence that constitutive Nrf2 activation confers cytoprotection to tumours, drug-efflux induction, chemoresistance and poor prognosis. Application here: Supplies the missing oncogenicity caveat for the Nrf2-activating candidates (X3, M2, M5), which currently carry "Tumorigenicity: Negligible"-style assertions with no basis. Any chronic CNS Nrf2 activator needs this risk stated.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Validation of the multiple sensor mechanism of the Keap1-Nrf2 system (2012). Transgenic Keap1-C151S rescue experiments showing that Cys151 is required for tBHQ, diethylmaleate, sulforaphane and dimethylfumarate, but dispensable for 15d-PGJ2, CDDO-Im, ebselen, nitro-oleic acid and cadmium — i.e. Keap1 has multiple, inducer-specific cysteine sensors. Application here: Use it to qualify the flat claim that curcumin acts via Cys151 (app.js:52, README.md:36), and it supplies the exact experiment (Keap1 C151S rescue) that should be specified to test the BTB arm of the mechanism separately from the Kelch decoy arm.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Neurodegenerative disease mutations in TREM2 reveal a functional surface and distinct loss-of-function mechanisms (2016). 3.1 Angstrom TREM2 Ig-like V-type domain structure showing that AD risk variants (including R47H) map to a surface that mediates ligand binding, while Nasu-Hakola mutations are buried and destabilise the fold. A companion 2018 J Biol Chem study (PDB 5UD7, 6B8O, primary citations retrieved from RCSB in this session) resolves the wild-type domain with phosphatidylserine bound. Application here: Ground truth for MOLBIO-09. Replace the invented "Arg47, Asp87, Lys112" set with residues from the published functional surface (Arg47 is genuinely on it; Ser112, not Lys112, is at position 112 and marks the domain boundary), and use the phosphatidylserine complex to state the true ligand chemistry — anionic lipid, not a cationic peptide.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: The TREM2 agonistic antibody AL002 in early Alzheimer's disease: a phase 2 randomized trial (2026). 381 participants with early AD, four arms, 48-96 weeks. Confirmed CNS target engagement (CSF sTREM2 down, osteopontin up) but the primary endpoint on CDR-SB was not met at any dose, and the most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events were MRI changes resembling ARIA. Application here: The essential clinical context missing from README.md:81/85 and app.js:303 ("Cytokine Storm Risk: Negligible"). It shows both that TREM2 agonism is achievable pharmacodynamically and that the clinical benefit is unproven and the safety profile is not benign — exactly the calibration the platform's TREM2 claims lack.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: A polarizing question: do M1 and M2 microglia exist? (2016). Argues that microglial polarization was never established by research findings, that the M1/M2 schema was imported from macrophage biology as an interpretive convenience, and that the terminology now hinders progress and should be discarded. Application here: Primary citation for MOLBIO-08. The entire microglia module (app.js:109-114, 297-345; README.md:80-85; index.html:186) needs rewriting around functional endpoints rather than M1/M2 poles.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Microglia states and nomenclature: A field at its crossroads (2022). Consensus paper from ~90 microglia investigators (Paolicelli, Sierra, Stevens, Tremblay, Colonna, Haass, Prinz, de Strooper, Ransohoff and others) providing a conceptual framework for microglial states as dynamic, and explicit nomenclature recommendations for researchers, reviewers and editors. Application here: Use its recommendations as the concrete rewriting guide for the microglia module: name the transcriptional state or the measured function, decouple state labels from assumed valence, and drop the good/bad dichotomy. Also resolves the M1 naming collision by forcing functional rather than categorical labels.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Impaired spatial learning after saturation of long-term potentiation (1998). Rats with no residual LTP capacity (<10%) after cross-bundle saturation were impaired in spatial learning, while animals retaining capacity for further potentiation were not. Application here: The decisive argument for MOLBIO-07: maximising LTP is not a coherent therapeutic objective because saturation occludes encoding. Cite it wherever "LTP +280%" appears, and replace the open-ended magnitude with a bounded target that preserves plasticity reserve.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: The efficacy and safety of donepezil in patients with Alzheimer's disease: results of a US multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (1996). Dose-response data linking plasma donepezil, red-blood-cell AChE inhibition and ADAS-cog change, with an inhibition plateau of 76-84% at plasma concentrations above 50 ng/mL. Application here: Quantitative anchor for MOLBIO-04. Shows that clinically effective cholinesterase inhibition is submaximal and plateaus, and gives the correct framing for replacing "completely blocks acetylcholine degradation" and "+350% synaptic ACh" with a defensible target inhibition range.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: An unaltered orthosteric site and a network of long-range allosteric interactions for PNU-120596 in alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (2015). Demonstrates that alpha-7 PAM action leaves the orthosteric agonist binding site unperturbed and operates through gating-interface and transmembrane residues that shift the gating equilibrium. Application here: Directly refutes the PfcACh-PAM-P1 design in MOLBIO-06, which lists the orthosteric aromatic box (Tyr188/Trp149/Tyr195) as the PAM site. Pair it with Targowska-Duda et al. 2018 (PMID 29363414 / doi:10.1080/07391102.2018.1427634), which localises type-II PAMs including PNU-120596 to an intrasubunit transmembrane cavity, to specify the correct allosteric site and to show why a hydrophilic peptide cannot reach it.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Molecular interactions of type I and type II positive allosteric modulators with the human alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor: an in silico study (2018). Docking and MD assignment of alpha-7 PAM sites: an intrasubunit transmembrane cavity recognising type-II PAMs (PNU-120596, PAM-2) with M1-Ser223 and M3-Ile281 as key contacts, an ECD site and an ECD-TMD junction site relevant to type-I PAMs, and an intersubunit pocket for 5-HI. Application here: Supplies the concrete alternative residue set for MOLBIO-06 if the authors wish to retain the PAM label, and establishes that the type-II site is intramembrane — the physical argument that a 41-mer hydrophilic peptide cannot be an alpha-7 type-II PAM.

tags: Molecular neurobiology / neuropharmacology — target biology, receptor structure-function, and mechanism-of-action claims
text: Structural basis of Wnt recognition by Frizzled (2012). XWnt8:mouse Fz8-CRD complex at 3.25 Angstrom. Two binding sites: a palmitoleic acid on the serine at the tip of the Wnt "thumb" inserting into a deep CRD groove, and hydrophobic contacts from the conserved "index finger" tip on the opposite CRD face. Application here: Refutes the "Wnt3a Loop" Frizzled-8 agonist design (app.js:173, README.md:63): the dominant interface is a covalently attached lipid that a synthetic peptide cannot reproduce, and the CKCHG segment the platform copied (badly) from WNT3A is not the CRD-binding element. Use it to redirect the FZD8 candidate toward a bivalent Wnt-surrogate architecture, which is the modality this structure enabled.
